Senses.Explanation: (劈箭急, swift as a splitting arrow) is a three-graph speed-cry the corpus never splits. Huqiu Shaolong answers a layer question with it, Yuanwu Keqin sets it over the turning year, Wuzhun Shifan over the lessening water of life, Koho Kennichi opens a hall address with it before the winter chicken standing alone, and Nouyun Zhenshi closes his ruling on the Yunmen three-ailments monk with it — and what is Caotang Chan? swift as a splitting arrow. Answers. Huqiu Shaolong, at the Zhangjiao monastery of Xuanzhou, is asked how it is when one layer is taken away by one layer — the dull bird leaves the nest; and how it is when one layer is not taken away by one layer — swift as a splitting arrow; pressed with Muzhou Daoming's yesterday-eggplant-today-wintermelon he answers eyes on the southeast, mind on the northwest, concedes the day's loss, and asks the assembly whether his answer saw Muzhou's intent at all. Shengke Deyu's ladder runs under-one's-own-body, manifest body, before leaving the abbot's room — watch with closed eyes — and after leaving, swift as a splitting arrow; the questioner spins empty space, laughs once, nothing to discuss, and sleeves back into the ranks; Shengke says do not say there is nothing to do. Nouyun Zhenshi, after the Yunmen three-ailments story wakes his monk — worship, the staff-thrust, are you not blind; come near, are you not deaf; do you understand, are you not mute — rules it down: this monk woke all right, but only to Yunmen-and-Xuansha Chan; to wake to Caotang Chan is very, very hard. And what is Caotang Chan? Swift as a splitting arrow. Time and season. Yuanwu Keqin's winter-month first-day address — day upon day swift as a splitting arrow, morning upon morning turning through the vast deep, good news for the human world; a shout of exertion, look higher yet, lest the head go grey in vain. Wuzhun Shifan, on the fifth day of the first month — the world's affairs tangled as hemp, time swift as a splitting arrow; therefore the day is past and life declines, what joy for the fish in the lessening water? — and yet the abbot wins only leaning on the railing all day, watching the clouds go by. Zishui's sixth-month address — heat wringing white sweat, the sun-crow carrying fire, the front hall's drum booming, the old ravine's flowing spring swift as a splitting arrow; the patriarch's intent already clear — do the two halls know it or not? Lianfeng Su, mid-seventh month — time swift as a splitting arrow, summer gone and autumn startling again; where the practitioner dwells and moves it is like an unmoored boat. Gulin Zhi's occasional-feeling instruction sighs the spring light away — swift as a splitting arrow, and suddenly it is past the first of winter. Verse. Tanfang Shouzhong's presentation verse for the abbot styled Guanxi Yin — Dragon Gate ten thousand fathoms high, Guanxi swift as a splitting arrow; the double pass thrown open, walk in with swinging arms, the wooden horse neighing at Cao Creek, the iron ox asleep at Shaolin. Dai'an Puzhuang sends off attendant Ru — the cheeping cry lands on the decisive moment, how much swifter than a splitting arrow! without borrowing thought, who speaks of stages? Zhangxue Tongzui glosses Yunmen Wenyan's reverse-say-one — mirror against mirror, space fitted to space, level clouds on the peaks — reverse-say-one, swift as a splitting arrow, Mount Sumeru ten thousand fathoms and no wall standing. Eryin Mi confers a name — eyes sharp as Shariputra's, wisdom-light called foremost; mechanism swift as the wind, tongue-debate swift as a splitting arrow, the Moye sword held level sweeping the sky blue. Hanxiu Ruqian, for the lineage nephew Zongnan — the truth-body red-rot, dripping fresh blood, the travelers failing to know it; only the transcending author knows the end-point — knowing the end-point, swift as a splitting arrow; the true conceals no false, the crooked hides no straight, a golden roc threaded through a needle's eye. Zhufeng Huanmin raises the coffin of senior seat Jiantang — the warm wind wafting the whole courtyard fragrant, the stroll far and long swift as a splitting arrow. The crossing and the anchor. In Japan, Koho Kennichi, heir of Wuxue Zuyuan, opens a hall address before the mechanism — swift as a splitting arrow; gather the spirit, still the thoughts, the winter chicken standing alone — the address after recorder Xie's whisk turn has lifted out the dragon horn and emptied the valley with a roar. And the claim anchor: the Five Lamps Complete Book's life of Huqiu Shaolong carries the same Zhangjiao exchange as his own record — the dull bird, then swift as a splitting arrow, then the Muzhou pressing — writing (師曰) where the record writes (師云)； kept only as the anchor, after the gate was met by fifteen Tier-2 rows across fifteen works, and never toward it.

Senses.Explanation: Its central named case addresses the immortal Lü Dongbin: after he asks about hiding a world in a grain and cooking mountains and rivers in a small pot, Huanglong Huinan points and says, “this corpse-guarding ghost” (這守屍鬼). Lü invokes a drug of deathlessness; Huanglong Huinan replies, “even after eighty thousand ages, in the end you fall into empty extinction” (饒經八萬劫，終是落空亡). Other Chan records apply the same epithet to sitting inert on a cushion, a tenth-stage sage, and anyone who lives a hundred or thousand years but remains “a corpse-guarding ghost; its ghost does not disperse; a dead person” (守屍鬼魂、不散底死人). Yet Gaofeng Yuanmiao also instructs someone to guard on and on like a corpse-guarding ghost until the doubt-clump bursts with a sound. The Chan deviation is the use of this macabre epithet across case verdict, criticism, and an attested simile in instruction. The differing appraisals are preserved rather than harmonized.

Senses.Explanation: Speakers use this paired verb phrase for a criticized arrest: sinking into emptiness and remaining stuck in stillness. Stored cases call it an illness, place it among explicit prohibitions, describe self-only concern that neglects living beings, or contrast it with treating the many things as absent. The Chinese Chan sources use it to identify a failure, not to name an activity they commend. Fozhi Duanyu sets two obstructions against each other: "if one teaching exists, layer upon layer of iron walls and silver mountains; if the myriad teachings are absent, everywhere one sinks into emptiness and sticks in stillness" (一法若有重重鐵壁銀山，萬法若無處處沈空滯寂). Gaofeng includes the phrase among a long series of proposed reasons for failure, asking, "is it sinking into emptiness and sticking in stillness?" (莫是沈空滯寂麼), before rejecting the whole diagnostic list as the answer. Yuansou says figures in an arhat painting "sink into emptiness and stick in stillness, know only their own completion, and do not attend to delivering living beings" (沈空滯寂，只知自了，不顧度生). Chushi explicitly calls it "the Chan illness of the two vehicles" (二乘禪病).

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 於胸中，曾無芥蔕。漲蜀江八千於舌上，儘有波瀾。問雙鞋子，甚處得來，積翠南，激揚機路活。拖條布裙，作屎臭氣。兜率悅，嗅著髑髏乾。一生弄大旗，策元勳於龍虵陣上。三關挫驢脚，馳十影於驥馬群間。末後句，教無盡，疑則別參，點行真藥。一轉語，住黃蘗，未曾夢見，打破疑團。老東山，背後贊揚，逢人頻合掌。薛大頭，面前遭喝，無地著慚顏。鴆毛本毒，虎體元班。妙處欲言言不及，月移花影上欄干。五祖演禪師五祖演禪師師諱法演，嗣白雲，緜州鄧氏子。初在成都聽講時，舉西天外道立義問佛弟子云：菩薩成道時，神與智冥，理與境會，不分能證所證，畢竟以何為證？弟子義墮，乃不鳴鐘鼓，從後門出入，返搭袈裟。三藏至再集，外道釋云：如人飲水，冷暖自知。道乃伏徵。諸法師云：冷暖固可知，未審自知之理如何？眾皆杜口。中有云：汝欲明此，須見南方明佛心宗者。師遂南來，至興元，經時逗留受業。師聞得，乃附書曰：汝出醬甕，復入虀瓮。師遂發。行至浮山，理此義，問山曰：如來有密語，迦葉不覆藏。師乃釋疑。山因指見白雲：師到，因問摩尼珠話，大悟，作投機頌曰：山前一片閑田地，叉手叮嚀問祖翁。幾度賣來還自買，為憐松竹引清風。雲印可之。示眾云：大凡參學，如俊鶻打鷯兒，纔洎地便飛去，若有蹲坐即不堪。小參，有云：某十有餘年海上參尋，見數人尊宿，自謂了當。及到浮山圓鑒會下，直是開口不得。後到白

Senses.Explanation: The monastic robe is the physical garment worn by a monk. Yongming Yanshou's authored compilation tells of a Buddha robe hung on a high standard and shown publicly. Gulin Qingmao's verse has the robe wrapped around the head. Xisou Shaotan's biographical narration has Wuzu Fayan wear the robe reversed after the defeated side leaves by the back door. Handling or displaying the same garment can carry institutional force, but these witnesses do not require a separate nonphysical sense.
